Earlier this year, Apple closed off part of the Apple Park Visitor Center, saying it was to "improve our store."

That space has now reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed the augmented reality experience that used custom iPads to let visitors see Apple Park.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, the company promoted the AR experience this way:

Using augmented reality technology, a three-dimensional model of the campus comes to life before your eyes, inviting guests to explore Apple Park in an immersive, interactive way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building and see one of the largest on-site solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof to peek at the layout of the collaborative workspace inside.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three areas: an AR exhibit, a traditional-format Apple Store, and a café.

Apple has now retired the AR exhibit and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. As MacRumors discovered, this includes a product wall running along the wall to display accessories, as well as redesigned display tables showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but nine years on, the space seems to have better uses.

I hope Apple isn't simply turning it into a regular retail store, but is thinking of other new ideas; at least the café is still there as a feature of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
